name: `SERVTUNER_BASE_PATH`
meaning: context path the UI is hosted under (`frontend.basePath`); validated at start, an invalid value stops the container. Served under this path and also at `/`, so an ingress may pass the prefix through or strip it

name: `SERVTUNER_SCHEMA_DIR`
meaning: directory of the RunSpec and event schemas (`schema/json`); the api image sets it, the chart does not

name: `SERVTUNER_API_PORT`
meaning: api listen port

name: `SERVTUNER_SECRET_STORE`
meaning: where saved targets' keys live (`secretStore`): Secrets in the runs namespace, files under the data directory (local development only), or nowhere

name: `SERVTUNER_RUN_SECRETS_DIR`
meaning: where a subprocess run or a target check gets the Secrets it names, as files for `servtuner run --secrets-dir`; deleted when the run or check ends. The chart mounts a memory-backed `emptyDir` there

name: `SERVTUNER_RUNNER`
meaning: runner implementation. The api's own default is `subprocess` (dev, single node, CI); the chart sets `kubernetes`

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_BINARY`
meaning: path to the `servtuner` binary; required for the `subprocess` runner

name: `SERVTUNER_API_URL`
meaning: URL bench uses to reach the api. Subprocess runner: default `https://localhost:<port>` (`http://` without TLS). Kubernetes runner: required; the chart sets the api Service, `<scheme>://<fullname>-api.<namespace>.svc:<port>`

name: `SERVTUNER_ENGINE_OVERRIDE`
meaning: **dev and e2e only, never set by the chart.** Passed to bench as `--engine-override`, so a run needs no real load engine

name: `SERVTUNER_RUNS_NAMESPACE`
meaning: namespace for bench Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`
meaning: ServiceAccount for bench Jobs

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_IMAGE`
meaning: bench image for Jobs

name: `SERVTUNER_IMAGE_REGISTRY`
meaning: `global.imageRegistry` without a trailing slash, or empty; offered as the registry of managed vLLM images

name: `SERVTUNER_OFFLINE`
meaning: `offline`: no public datasheet fallback, AWS pricing refused; passed to bench Jobs

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_CPU`, `_MEMORY`
meaning: the bench pod's requests, equal to its limits (Guaranteed QoS); `bench.resources`

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_TARGET_ANTI_AFFINITY`
meaning: keep the bench pod off the nodes of the workloads under test (`target.workload` and every upstream's); `bench.targetAntiAffinity`

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_JOB_TTL_SECONDS`
meaning: `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` of bench Jobs; the spec ConfigMap and token Secret are owned by the Job and go with it

name: `SERVTUNER_BENCH_START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
meaning: a bench pod that has not started by then (unschedulable, image pull failing) fails the run with the reason, and its Job is deleted

name: `SERVTUNER_IMAGE_PULL_SECRETS`
meaning: `global.imagePullSecrets` and `imagePullSecrets` names for bench pods, comma-separated, each once

name: `SERVTUNER_DATA_FS_GROUP`
meaning: the bench pod's `fsGroup`, so it can write the data volume (`api.fsGroup`)

name: `SERVTUNER_PROMETHEUS_URL`
meaning: Prometheus base URL, used as a RunSpec default

name: `SERVTUNER_TUNING_MONITOR`
meaning: How Prometheus finds a managed vLLM: `podmonitor` (Prometheus Operator) or `scrape-annotations` (community chart), from `tuning.monitor`

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_MODE`
meaning: User auth: `local` checks every route; `none` checks nothing, the explicit opt-out

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_METHODS`
meaning: How users sign in under `local`, in chain order

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_SETUP_TOKEN_FILE`
meaning: The setup token that creates the first admin (read from a Secret file, never stored); without it no admin can be created

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS`
meaning: A session ends after this long unused

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_SECONDS`
meaning: A session ends this long after sign-in, whatever its use

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE`
meaning: `false` only for a plain-HTTP install not on localhost: the cookie then loses `Secure` and the `__Host-` prefix

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_LOCKOUT_MAX_FAILURES`
meaning: Failed logins per username before it is locked

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS`
meaning: The window failures are counted in, and how long the lock lasts

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_FORWARD_USER_HEADER`
meaning: The header the trusted proxy names the user in (forward_header)

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_FORWARD_DISPLAY_NAME_HEADER`
meaning: Optional header with a new user's display name

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_FORWARD_EMAIL_HEADER`
meaning: Optional header with a new user's email

name: `SERVTUNER_AUTH_FORWARD_PROVISIONING`
meaning: What a forwarded subject with no servtuner user gets

name: `SERVTUNER_TUNING_NAMESPACES`
meaning: Namespaces where managed vLLM targets may be stored and deployed, from `rbac.tuning.namespaces`; unset grants none

name: `SERVTUNER_STORAGE_BACKEND`
meaning: bundle store

name: `SERVTUNER_DATA_DIR`
meaning: data directory (file backend)

name: `SERVTUNER_DATA_CLAIM`
meaning: PVC to mount in Jobs at the data directory (file backend)

name: `SERVTUNER_STORAGE_NODE_PINNED`
meaning: data volume is RWO, so Jobs must share the api's node

name: `SERVTUNER_API_COMPONENT_LABEL`
meaning: `key=value` label selecting the api pod, for the runner's RWO pod affinity

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_ENDPOINT`, `_REGION`, `_BUCKET`, `_PREFIX`
meaning: S3 location (s3 backend; endpoint empty for AWS)

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE`
meaning: path-style addressing

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_CHECKSUM_MODE`
meaning: checksum behaviour

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_PART_SIZE_MIB`
meaning: multipart part size for uploads (`storage.s3.partSizeMiB`)
values: whole MiB, at least 5; default 16. A larger file goes up in parts, aborted on failure
readBy: bench (the api passes it to Jobs)

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_PRESIGN`
meaning: download links (`storage.s3.presign`)
values: `true`: `GET /runs/{id}/files/{path}` answers 307 to a 5-minute presigned GET (SigV4); `false` (default): the api streams the file

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_CREDENTIALS_SECRET`, `_ACCESS_KEY_KEY`, `_SECRET_KEY_KEY`
meaning: the Secret (in the runs namespace) and the two keys bench Jobs read `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` from, by reference; credentials source `secret` only

name: `SERVTUNER_S3_CREDENTIALS_SOURCE`
meaning: credential source

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_ENABLED`
meaning: whether connections use TLS: each connection's default, never inferred

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`
meaning: the api listener's client-certificate policy (`ingressApi`, `benchApi`); bench presents its certificate unless it is `none`

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_CONNECTION_BENCH_API`, `_BENCH_PROMETHEUS`, `_INGRESS_API`, `_OBJECT_STORE`, `_POSTGRES`
meaning: whether each connection uses TLS, overriding `SERVTUNER_TLS_ENABLED`. With TLS, each component presents its one certificate; the server decides whether to ask for it
readBy: api; runner passes bench's connections to Jobs

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_CERT_FILE`, `SERVTUNER_TLS_KEY_FILE`
meaning: api certificate and key (mounted `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret)
values: path; set only when a connection uses the api's certificate

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE`
meaning: private CA the api listener verifies client certificates against (never the combined bundle, which admits public CAs). Default: `ca.crt` beside `SERVTUNER_TLS_CERT_FILE`. The chart sets it when the api listener checks client certificates (TLS, and `tls.clientAuth` not `none`), pointing at the `ca.crt` of the CA Secret (`tls.caSecretRef`, else the api certificate Secret)
values: path; only when client certificates are checked

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_BENCH_SECRET`
meaning: name of the bench client-certificate Secret, in the runs namespace
values: Secret name; set only when needed

name: `SERVTUNER_TLS_CA_SECRET`
meaning: Secret in the runs namespace whose `ca.crt` verifies the api for bench (`servtuner run --tls-ca-file`): `tls.caSecretRef`, else the bench Secret (cert-manager writes the issuing CA into it). With `tls.caSecretRef` and a separate runs namespace, that Secret must exist in the runs namespace too
values: Secret name; only when the bench-api connection uses TLS

name: `POD_NAMESPACE`
meaning: the api pod's namespace (downward API), for the RWO pod affinity to the api pod

name: `SSL_CERT_FILE`
meaning: combined system + private CA bundle built by the init container
values: `/etc/servtuner/ca/bundle.crt`; set only when some connection uses TLS

name: `SERVTUNER_DATABASE_HOST`, `_PORT`, `_NAME`, `_USER`
meaning: Postgres connection

name: `SERVTUNER_DATABASE_SSLMODE`
meaning: Postgres TLS; must agree with the postgres connection

name: `SERVTUNER_DATABASE_AUTH`
meaning: how the api signs in to Postgres (chart `postgres.auth`): its client certificate, whose CN is the user (needs TLS), or a password

name: `SERVTUNER_DATABASE_PASSWORD`
meaning: database password; set only with `SERVTUNER_DATABASE_AUTH=password`

name: `X-Forwarded-Prefix`
meaning: Context path from a proxy that strips its prefix. For that request it overrides `SERVTUNER_BASE_PATH`. The rule is in `frontend/nginx.conf.template`: each segment is 1 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` and is not `.` or `..`. An invalid value, or a duplicated header, is ignored and the env path is used.
